payload.reason: The evidence indicates a correlation between daytime activity and socioeconomic status, suggesting that being active during the day is associated with higher socioeconomic status and the use of more standard language.

claims.text: People active during the day have higher average income than those active at night, indicating a link between daytime activity and socioeconomic status.
Standard language usage is more prevalent during the daytime, while non-standard variants are more common at night, suggesting that time of activity influences linguistic standards.
The variability in language use is explained by the socioeconomic status of users active at different times of day, supporting the connection between daytime activity and SEC.
